title.narrative: Scaling Up Renewable Energy Technologies for Agri-Food Value Chain Transformation in Kiambu County

description.narrative: Overall Object : Food and nutrition security of farming families in Kiambu district is improved through the use of renewable energy technologies in the agriculture value chain.Specific Objective/Outcome: 3000 smallholder farmers and 150 value chain actors apply sustainable renewable energy technologies to agri-food value chains and will provide a more balanced diet for themselves and their families.

The primary direct target group is 100 farmer-owned producer groups with 3,000 smallholder dairy and horticulture farms in three sub-counties and 15 districts, namely Githunguri (Githunguri, Githiga, Ikinu and Ngewa), Limuru (Bibirioni, Limuru Central, Ndeiya, Limuru East, Ngecha and Tigoni) and Kikuyu (Karai, Nachu, Sigona, Kikuyu and Kinoo). By gender, 60% of the target group will be women and 20% will be youth. The selection of the target group will be participatory by ADS-Kenya with the involvement of the community, County Government Department of Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries and Cooperatives and the Department of Water, Environment, Energy and Natural Resources and the technical consultants who conducted the feasibility study. The secondary direct target group consists of 150 value chain actors, which include:40 agribusinesses (agricultural traders, product collection and storage centers, processing centers, retailers),40 Government stakeholders (energy regulator, agricultural extension officers/interns, and policy makers in district assemblies),10 financial institutions ( commercial banks, microfinance institutions, government affirmative action funds, e.g., women's enterprise funds and youth funds,10 Research and educational institutions (universities, research organizations, e.g., Kenya Agriculture and Livestock Research Organization, Institute for Energy Studies and Research, technical and vocational schools),20 civil society organizations at the macro, meso, and micro levels (local producer associations, agricultural cooperatives, community-based organizations, Kenya Climate Change Working Group Association, Kenya National Farmers Federation, Kenya Renewable Energy Association, Kenya Young Greens) and 30 renewable energy technicians, 50% of whom are women

The project is a strategic initiative aimed at catalyzing the widespread adoption of renewable energy technologies (Solar and Biogas) in the horticulture and Dairy Value chain in Kiambu County. It seeks to address energy-related challenges within the agri-food industry by promoting the use of clean and sustainable energy sources.By developing and implementing innovative solutions, providing training and capacity-building for stakeholders, and influencing policy changes, this project aspires to enhance energy efficiency, reduce environmental impact, and boost productivity across the entire agri-food value chain, from farm to table, ultimately fostering sustainable and resilient agricultural practices while contributing to broader environmental and economic sustainability goals.
